links.outcome: Association of AI trust and usage frequency with delayed or cancelled care-seeking
links.effect: Higher AI trust associated with delay (adjusted OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18); usage frequency OR 1.39; 11.6% (285/2460) deferred or cancelled care due to AI advice.
links.quote: In the fully adjusted model (model 4), AI trust remained a significant predictor (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18; P =.04; Figure 2 B).

links.outcome: Over-trust in AI advice leading to delayed care, with false reassurance
links.effect: Predicted delay probability rose from 11.6% at baseline to 30.5% with high trust and high frequency, and 35.8% adding chronic illness.
links.quote: Combining high trust and high frequency led to a delay probability of 30.5%, and when all 3 factors—high trust, high frequency, and chronic illness—were present, the probability escalated to 35.8%.

unlisted_practices: Simulated (agent-based) broadcast risk messaging to reduce AI-related care delay

links.outcome: postponed or canceled care due to AI advice
links.quote: In terms of health care decision outcomes, 11.6% (285/2460) of participants deferred or canceled health care due to AI advice, while 18.9% (465/2460) changed their health care decisions based on it.

links.effect: Broadcast reduced delay odds vs baseline: OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.94-0.95; P <.001.
links.quote: Compared to the baseline, the broadcast strategy significantly reduced the odds of delay (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.94-0.95; P <.001).
